payload.raw: Default styling contract

The renderer emits semantic markup and stable renderer classes such as `.markdown-v2-output`, `.markdown-list`, `.markdown-list-item`, `.markdown-code-block`, and `.markdown-link`. It does not inject CSS at runtime.

payload.raw: Block-level overrides

payload.highlightedHtml:
import { StreamingMarkdown } from "stream-mdx";
import { ScrollAreaHorizontal } from "@/components/ui/scroll-area";

const components = {
  code: ({ html }) => (
    <pre className="not-prose docs-code-block">
      <ScrollAreaHorizontal className="min-w-auto">
        <div className="min-w-max p-4" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
      </ScrollAreaHorizontal>
    </pre>
  ),
};

export function StyledCode({ text }: { text: string }) {
  return <StreamingMarkdown text={text} components={components} worker="/workers/markdown-worker.js" />;
}

payload.raw: This wraps the optimized code rendering inside a horizontal scroll container while keeping the patch pipeline intact. The wrapper class is intentionally app-owned; do not treat it as a default visual prescription for other projects.

payload.raw: Code highlighting themes
StreamMDX provides end-to-end configurable Shiki themes for code blocks. Pass any Shiki bundled theme name for light and dark modes:

inline.text: StreamMDX provides end-to-end configurable Shiki themes for code blocks. Pass any Shiki bundled theme name for light and dark modes:

payload.highlightedHtml:
<StreamingMarkdown
  text={content}
  themes={{ light: "min-light", dark: "nord" }}
/>

payload.raw: Themes are loaded on demand into the worker highlighter singleton, and cache partitions prevent cross-contamination between engines with different themes. Unknown or invalid theme names report an initialization error through the standard error callback and fall back safely to default GitHub themes.

payload.raw: Inline overrides
Inline overrides let you swap tags for specific inline nodes:

inline.text: Inline overrides let you swap tags for specific inline nodes:

payload.highlightedHtml:
const inlineComponents = {
  code: ({ text }: { text: string }) => <code className="inline-code">{text}</code>,
  link: ({ href, children }: { href?: string; children: React.ReactNode }) => (
    <a className="markdown-link" href={href} target={href?.startsWith("http") ? "_blank" : undefined}>
      {children}
    </a>
  ),
};

<StreamingMarkdown text={content} inlineComponents={inlineComponents} />;

payload.raw: Use inline overrides to preserve the semantic role while delegating the final visual treatment to your prose stylesheet.

inline.text: Use inline overrides to preserve the semantic role while delegating the final visual treatment to your prose stylesheet.

payload.raw: Tables
Table rendering can use custom elements:

inline.text: Table rendering can use custom elements:

payload.highlightedHtml:
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@/components/ui/table";

const tableElements = {
  Table,
  Thead: TableHeader,
  Tbody: TableBody,
  Tr: TableRow,
  Th: TableHead,
  Td: TableCell,
};

<StreamingMarkdown text={content} tableElements={tableElements} />;

payload.raw: This swaps table tags without changing how the renderer schedules updates.

inline.text: This swaps table tags without changing how the renderer schedules updates.

payload.raw: HTML overrides
When `features.html` is enabled, HTML blocks can be mapped onto custom components:

inline.text: is enabled, HTML blocks can be mapped onto custom components:

payload.highlightedHtml:
const htmlElements = {
  table: ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => <div className="not-prose overflow-x-auto">{children}</div>,
  blockquote: ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => <blockquote>{children}</blockquote>,
};

<StreamingMarkdown text={content} htmlElements={htmlElements} features={{ html: true }} />;
